name: motion-craft
description: Make short videos from code, the way Claude Motion does, with open tools that run on your own machine: animated explainers, launch and feature films, data stories from a spreadsheet, logo stings, transparent overlays, vertical social clips, product demos and 3D or simulation pieces. HTML compositions render frame by frame through HeyGen's open-source HyperFrames, pinned to a tested release and run locally with telemetry off and no account, plus a bundled procedural sound engine mastered to -14 LUFS. A director before an animator: it reads the subject and gathers its real logo, screens and numbers, writes three storylines and a spec that turns every adjective into a number with a banned-defaults list, designs the rhythm (hook inside 3 s, the hero on the strongest beat) around one carried element and the subject's own signature device, applies a finishing pass (motion blur, 60 fps, grain, depth), reviews contact sheets, full-rate transition strips, a single-frame pop scan and phone-width frames against measured craft numbers, and leaves the film editable through variables and stable element ids in a live preview. Every rule traces to 18 video transcripts, 10 open-source motion skills and engines, frame-by-frame measurements of two reference films, a 48-film study of shipped SaaS product films, and measurements of 240 gallery films made with Claude, 21 product films made from websites, and one fund-administration company's films and interface loops.
